newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ economy softer than expected - Bank of N.Zealand.
newsitem.headline: NZ economy softer than expected - Bank of N.Zealand.

text.p: The New Zealand economy has softened more than expected and expectations for recovery had been shifted back to the fourth quarter, the Bank of New Zealand said in a quarterly outlook published on Thursday.

The bank said in its May quarter outlook for fixed interest that it expects the Reserve Bank of New Zealand to ease the level of desired conditions by 50-75 basis points in its June Monetary Policy Statement -- an outcome largely priced into the market.
A cyclical upturn was not yet underway but an outlook for an acceleration in growth at some point still seems reasonable, it said.
The bank said that on balance New Zealand would remain an attractive market for international investors but near-term risks to the downside for the economy remained strong.
"While some downside risks are clear for the New Zealand currency, we see these as only being mild for the remainder of 1997," it said.
"The economy is clearly still slowing, with the latest run of first quarter data looking particularly weak," the bank said.
"Critically, the source of the anticiated economic recovery -- domestic consumption and investment -- remain subdued."
Retail sales had been flat, housing starts had slowed, employment and hours worked fell in the March quarter.
Negative GDP growth appeared assured for the March quarter, the bank said.
The bank said overly tight monetary conditions were the culprit for the slowdown.
An easing would clearly depend on inflation and BNZ does not believe the underlying inflation rate would drop below 1.0 percent while the economy continued to grow.
The bank said the balance of risks suggested the economy would underperform and, should this be the case, there could be a further easing after the June Monetary Policy Statement.
